topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: Well, now, isn’t this a curious turn of the spade? I tell you, it’s like finding a sweet apple in the middle of a dry winter. My old friend, he’s come back to the village, and yet he doesn’t carry the faces of the past in his mind. But what does it matter? The sun still shines, and the soil still welcomes the seed. It’s a chance to sow new memories, like planting rows of fresh turnips. We can speak of the harvests to come and the saints to pray to. I reckon it’s not losing a friend but gaining one anew. The past is the past, and the future is a field ripe for the plowing.
